research.text: The research focuses on discovering and developing fundamentally new optical-based imaging technologies for in vivo visualization of tissue at both macroscopic and microscopic scales. By integrating optics with advanced computational approaches, novel imaging tools are created to detect cancers, map brain activities, probe inflammations, and guide cancer therapies in both animals and humans.

research.text: I am a tenure-track assistant professor at the University of South Florida (USF) conducting research on dry eye disease with multiple optical imaging techniques. During my PhD studies, I primarily focused on utilizing broadband, ultrashort laser pulses for complementary contrast mechanisms in multimodal microscopy (supervised by Dr. Alvin T. Yeh). During that time, I developed a multimodal imaging platform, integrating multiphoton microscopy (MPM) with optical coherence tomography (OCT) techniques, for intravital studies of biological processes and responses within 3D living tissues. As a result of that interdisciplinary research between biomedical science and engineering, I gained significant experience in nonlinear optics, optical microscopy, cell culture, tissue engineering, and biomechanics.
